setup_steps: Read build.gradle and .github/workflows/gradle.yml: the project targets Java 21 (the enforcer caps bytecode at 21), CI uses Temurin 21 and runs ./gradlew build. The machine only had JDK 17 (plus Homebrew openjdk 25).
Installed JDK 21 with `brew install openjdk@21`. JAVA_HOME is /opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home.
Ran `./gradlew test` with JAVA_HOME set to JDK 21. The Gradle wrapper downloaded Gradle 9.8.2 and the dependencies from Maven Central.
Also ran `./gradlew build` (the CI command, which adds checkstyle). It passed.
No external services needed: the tests use in-memory/H2 storage and mocks. The traccar-web submodule and tools/test-integration.py (needs a running server) are not part of the automated suite.
result.summary: The environment is set up with Homebrew OpenJDK 21 and the Gradle 9.8.2 wrapper. `./gradlew test` passes: 428 test classes, 612 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 27 skipped. The skipped tests are disabled on purpose in the source because they call external services (geocoder, geolocation, map matcher, mail, Overpass and similar). The full `./gradlew build` with checkstyle also passes. I did not need a database or any other service. I left the system default Java (17) unchanged, so the test command sets JAVA_HOME explicitly. `--rerun` makes the test task run again even if Gradle considers it up to date.
